notice: Invented paper scenarios only. No tickets, keys, directory exports, credentials, packet captures or executed domain observations are present.

observations: A fictional Helpdesk group has a scoped reset permission for TrainingUsers only.
No control over other containers or privileged objects is supplied.
cases.claim: Helpdesk controls every account in the forest.

observations: The scenario explicitly grants one invented user read access to their own application record.
That particular read is supplied as completed.
A fictional client has a TGT in its cache.
No target-service exchange or resource permission is supplied.
cases.claim: The client is authorised to read every service record.

observations: The fictional KDC has issued a ticket for the selected service.
No service acceptance or application response is supplied.
cases.claim: The application has accepted the client and returned its data.

observations: The fictional service is explicitly said to have authenticated the client.
Its separate policy forbids reading another user's private record.
cases.claim: Authentication permits reading that other record.

observations: The supplied diagnostic reports a clock-related validation problem.
The exact credential and other protocol checks have not been established.
The supplied service-name resolution attempt failed.
No completed exchange with the intended KDC/service is supplied.
cases.claim: The KDC denied this user's resource permissions.

observations: A supplied ticket request failed and the intended service-principal mapping is unresolved.
No unique failure cause is established.
cases.claim: The service secret is the only possible cause.

observations: The fictional application policy permits the selected subject to read one training report.
That exact read is supplied as completed; no edit was attempted.
cases.claim: The selected read succeeded; edit permission remains unknown.

observations: The scenario records client authentication at a service.
The client-side evidence needed to establish server authentication is absent.
cases.claim: Mutual authentication is proven in both directions.

observations: A fictional learner proposes publishing ticket/session-key material after hiding a display name.
No actual ticket or key is included in the dataset and no sharing approval is supplied.
cases.claim: Removing the display name makes that material safe to publish.

observations: The supplied approved brief covers the earlier clean workgroup Windows exercise only.
Domain installation, join, directory querying and ticket operations are not approved.
cases.claim: The learner may now join the guest to a domain and inspect tickets.
